lines.japanese: 「つーかおまえ、何しに来たの」
lines.english: “Anyway, what are you doing here?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええーとですね……それはほら、クレープを食しに来たに決まってるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “W-well, you see... Obviously I came to partake of a crêpe.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でもクレープ買ってないじゃん。買おうともしなかったじゃん」
lines.english: “But you didn't buy one. You never even tried.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は俺の視線を避けて、夜の花水木通りをおのぼりの観光客みたいにぐーっと見渡した。
lines.english: Avoiding my gaze, Naru swept her eyes over Flowering Dogwood Street like a country tourist gawking at the city for the first time.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうですねー、えー、クレープを食すというのは副次行動でしてー、基本的には自転車を探していましたねー」
lines.english: “Well, yes. Partaking of a crêpe was a secondary objective. Primarily, I was searching for the bicycle.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。あの辺りもうさんざん探しつくしてんじゃん。おまえさ、そーゆー効率わりぃ探し方すんなよ」
lines.english: “Why? You’ve already searched that whole area inside and out. Quit going about it so inefficiently.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、屋台のラーメン美味しそー」
lines.english: “Oh, that street-stall ramen looks delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい女、聞け。いまこのおにいさん、ためになる話してんぞ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, woman, listen. This gentleman is trying to teach you something useful.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえいえそんな。ダイエット中ですからお構いなく」
lines.english: “Oh, no, no. Don't trouble yourself. I'm on a diet.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、おごるなんて話はしてねえよ」
lines.english: “I never offered to buy you any.”

lines.japanese: 「だいたいおまえダイエットって。そんな脆弱な体してるくせに、それ以上痩せおとろえる必要はねーだろ」
lines.english: “And what do you mean, diet? You're already built like a stiff breeze could kill you. You don't need to waste away any further.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやー、それが美の追求に終着点はないんですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. You see, the pursuit of beauty has no final destination.”

lines.japanese: やつは首を傾け、垂れていた髪を耳にかけた。
lines.english: She cocked her head and tucked a fallen lock of hair behind her ear.

lines.japanese: 「女を分かってないわね、坊や」
lines.english: “You don't understand women, little boy.”

lines.japanese: 「はふん！」
lines.english: “Hmph!”

lines.japanese: 俺はてのひらでやつの後頭部をはたいてやった。
lines.english: I smacked the back of her head with my palm.

lines.japanese: 「つーかさ、ダイエットっつーわりに、おまえいつもクレープとか普通にガン食いしてね」
lines.english: “Besides, for somebody on a diet, don't you routinely wolf down crêpes and stuff?”

lines.japanese: 「あーあーあー」
lines.english: “Ah-ah-ah-ah.”

lines.japanese: 「耳塞いだって体重は減らねーよ」
lines.english: “Covering your ears won't make you lose weight.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうなんですけどー、ドラさんしっかり突っこんでくれるから、私も安心してぼけられるんですよねー」
lines.english: “True. But you always give me a proper comeback, Dora. That makes it safe for me to play the fool.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえのはボケじゃねーだろ、天然」
lines.english: “You don't say stupid things on purpose. They come naturally.”

lines.japanese: 「計算！　計算！」
lines.english: “I plan it! I plan all of it!”

lines.japanese: 鳴はぶるんぶるん首を振って力説した。
lines.english: Naru whipped her head back and forth as she insisted.

lines.japanese: 「やめろやめろ。あんま脳みそシェイクすんな。悪化すんぞ」
lines.english: “Stop that. Don't shake your brain too hard. You'll make it worse.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、そうですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, you’re right.”
“...Worse?”

lines.japanese: まんまるい目で睨まれたがシカトした。
lines.english: She glared at me with round eyes. I ignored her.

lines.japanese: 「いちいち止まんな。歩け」
lines.english: “Quit stopping every five seconds. Walk.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 「……あれ、えーと」
lines.english: “...Wait, um...”

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「いま、なんの話でしたっけ？」
lines.english: “What were we talking about again?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。おまえが激太りしてるっつー話じゃん」
lines.english: “Dunno. I think it was about you getting massively fat.”

lines.japanese: 「し、してませんよ、そんな話！」
lines.english: “I-I am not! That wasn't what we were talking about!”

lines.japanese: 「して……してない……してない……」
lines.english: “I'm not... I'm not... I'm not...”

lines.japanese: 呟きながら腹の肉をつまんで見下ろしたりしている。不健康なぐらいひょろけてるくせに、美の追求云々は本気だったのかもしれない。
lines.english: Muttering, she pinched the flesh of her stomach and stared down at it. She was so spindly she looked unhealthy, but perhaps all that talk of pursuing beauty had been sincere.

lines.japanese: 「あそ。じゃ、いいな」
lines.english: “Okay. Then we're good.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なにがですかー？」
lines.english: “Huh? What is?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、せっかくだから、そこのラーメン食ってこうかと思──」
lines.english: “Since we're here, I was thinking we could eat at that ramen stand—”

lines.japanese: がしっ！
lines.english: Yank!

lines.japanese: 結構な腕力で袖を引かれた。
lines.english: She yanked my sleeve with surprising strength.
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「戻りましょう」
lines.english: “Let's go back.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　だって、おまえ減量中なんだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? But you're trying to lose weight, aren't you?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は神妙な表情で、小さく「前へならえ」するみたいに両手で数センチの空間を作ったあと、それを真横へ向けて放物線状にうっちゃった。
lines.english: With a solemn expression, Naru held her hands a few inches apart in a miniature arms-forward pose, then turned that little measure sideways and lobbed it away in an arc.

lines.japanese: 俺たちは無言で見つめあう。
lines.english: We gazed at each other in silence.

lines.japanese: 「……美の追求に終着点はないんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “...I thought the pursuit of beauty had no final destination.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、よく考えたら、ルーベンスもルノワールもふくよかな女のひとを描いてるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “On reflection, Rubens and Renoir both painted full-figured women, didn't they?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねえよ。どこの喫茶店だ」
lines.english: “How should I know? What coffee shops are those?”

lines.japanese: 「つまりスレンダーな曲線のみ至高とする美意識は、視野狭窄な現代人のおろかな幻想とも言えるのではないでしょうか」
lines.english: “In other words, the modern fixation on slender curves as the highest form of beauty may be nothing more than a narrow-minded delusion.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、ラーメン食いたいなら食いたいって言えよ」
lines.english: “If you want ramen, just say you want ramen.”

lines.japanese: 「食いたい」
lines.english: “I want ramen.”

lines.japanese: 「と、私どものルーベンスが申しております」
lines.english: “Or so says the Rubens inside me.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがねえなあ」
lines.english: “You're hopeless.”

lines.japanese: 俺はきびすを返し、一度は通りすぎた屋台へ向かった。都合がいい。どのみち時間を潰す必要があった。
lines.english: I turned on my heel and headed back toward the stall we had passed. It suited me. I needed to kill time anyway.

lines.japanese: 「きゃっほーう」
lines.english: “Yaaay!”

lines.japanese: 鳴はすぐに俺を追いこして一歩先を位置どった。
lines.english: Naru immediately darted past me to take the lead by one step.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうだ、ドラさんどう思いますー？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. What do you think, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「なにが」
lines.english: “About what?”

lines.japanese: 「ダ・ヴィンチのモナリザってー、モデルとなった女性について諸説あるじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “You know how there are several theories about the woman who sat for Leonardo da Vinci's *Mona Lisa*?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あーほら、人妻とか母親とかパトロンの愛人とかー、果ては女装したダビンチ自身なんて説もあるくらいですけどー」
lines.english: “Some say a married woman, some his mother, some his patron's mistress. Some even claim it was da Vinci himself in women's clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: ……なんで唐突に絵の話なんかしてんだ、こいつ。
lines.english: ...Why had she suddenly started talking about paintings?

lines.japanese: 「でもー、私思うんですけどー、あれは特定できない誰かであることこそあの絵の本質であってところでダシは鳥ガラですか？　豚の背脂ですか？」
lines.english: “But I think the impossibility of pinning her down is the very essence of the painting and by the way is the broth chicken stock or pork back fat?”

lines.japanese: すげえ。自由人だ。自由過ぎる。こいつと会話するのには、相手の言葉を適当に聞きながす才能が求められると分かった。
lines.english: Amazing. A free spirit. Far too free. I realized that talking to her required a talent for letting most of what she said wash straight past me.

lines.japanese: 「……動物系・魚介系ダブルスープ」
lines.english: “...Double broth. Meat stock and seafood stock.”

lines.japanese: 「ダブルスープ！」
lines.english: “Double broth!”

lines.japanese: 鳴はＶサインをふたつ繋げてＷサインを作った。
lines.english: Naru joined two V-signs into a W.

lines.japanese: 「くはー、そう来たかー！　ふゎー、美味しそー。へへー、わくわくしますねー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, so that's the answer! God, that sounds good. Heh-heh, this is exciting.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。良かったな」
lines.english: “I see. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 適当に聞きながす才能。
lines.english: The talent of half-listening.

lines.japanese: 「あと私ー、モナリザの表情から察するに、あの『微笑』っていうのは『微かな笑み』ではなく『微妙な笑み』のことだと──うあー、いー匂いしてきましたねー」
lines.english: “And judging by the *Mona Lisa's* expression, I think ‘subtle smile’ refers not to the faintness of the smile but to its ambiguity—ooh, that smells wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。良かったな」
lines.english: “I see. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 適当に聞きながす才能。
lines.english: The talent of half-listening.

lines.japanese: そしてそれ以降、俺たちの会話にダビンチだかサノバビッチだかが出てくることはなかった。
lines.english: From that point onward, neither da Vinci nor any son of a bitch appeared in our conversation again.

lines.japanese: 「ところで私ー、割りバシ割るのけっこう上手いんですよー」
lines.english: “By the way, I’m pretty good at splitting disposable chopsticks.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。良かったな」
lines.english: “I see. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 「ところで私ー、ルーベンスの絵の中でー」
lines.english: “Incidentally, among Rubens's paintings, I—”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。良かったな」
lines.english: “I see. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 屋台の横には、寒さと空腹にこたえるあったかい香りを挟んで、使いこまれた木製のテーブルが据えられていた。
lines.english: Beside the stall, beyond a bank of warm aromas irresistible to anyone cold and hungry, stood a battered wooden table.

lines.japanese: カウンター席の方は、すでに安物スーツのおっさんが三人陣取っている。俺と鳴は、テーブル席の片端に向かい合わせで座った。古びた丸椅子が音を立てて軋んだ。
lines.english: Three men in cheap suits had already occupied the counter. Naru and I sat facing each other at one end of the table. The old round stools creaked beneath us.

lines.japanese: 話（を一方的に聞くのが）好きな店主は、カウンター席の宝くじ談義に耳を傾けていて、まだ新しい来客に気付いちゃいない。
lines.english: The owner liked conversation—by which I meant listening to other people have one—and was absorbed in the counter customers' discussion of the lottery. He had yet to notice us.

lines.japanese: 「メンマ」
lines.english: “Menma.”

lines.japanese: 人差し指の第二間接でテーブルを大きく二度叩くと、ラグビー選手みたいにガタイのいい角刈りの男が屋台のフレームの中からじろりと俺を見た。
lines.english: I rapped the table twice with the second knuckle of my index finger. A burly man with a crew cut, built like a rugby player, glared at me from inside the stall.

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: メンマはいつもの仏頂面で常連客を迎えたが、初顔の子供には少しだけ柔らかい声を投げた。
lines.english: Menma greeted me, a regular, with his usual scowl, but gave the unfamiliar kid a marginally gentler welcome.

lines.japanese: 「らっしゃい」
lines.english: “Welcome.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は口を開けたままぺこりと会釈して、その驚いた顔を俺に持ちこして囁いた。
lines.english: Naru bowed with her mouth still open, brought her startled face close to mine, and whispered.

lines.japanese: 「はぇー、ドラさんお知り合いだったんですか？」
lines.english: “Oh. You know him, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「あーほら、前に話したろ。パルさんとか黒いオカマと会ったラーメン屋。それがここ」
lines.english: “Remember the ramen place I told you about, where I met Paru and the Black Queen? This is it.”

lines.japanese: 親指でまず下方向を二回突き、次に若い店主の方へ向けた。
lines.english: I jabbed my thumb downward twice, then pointed it toward the young proprietor.

lines.japanese: 「あの老けた兄ちゃんはメンマ。見た目怖えーけど、貧乏人に優しいんだよ。ラーメン一杯で何時間いても追いだされねーの」
lines.english: “That old-looking guy is Menma. He looks scary, but he’s kind to people down on their luck. You can sit here for hours over one bowl and he won’t throw you out.”

lines.japanese: その仇名の由来は麺の上にのっける竹の子のアレじゃなくて、ラーメンＭＡＮが略されてゆえのメンマ。まだ二十代だけど、行列が出来る有名店で頑固親父にシゴかれながら七年間修行を積んだだけあって腕は確かだ。
lines.english: The nickname didn't come from the bamboo shoots served on noodles. It was *ramen man* shortened into Menma. He was still in his twenties, but after seven years under a stubborn old master at a famous shop with lines out the door, his skill was unquestionable.

lines.japanese: 八年目がなかったのは頑固親父をフルボッコにしちゃったせいらしい。詳しいことまでは聞いてないけど、滅多なことで手を上げるようなやつじゃない。若さゆえのご愛敬ってことにしておいてやろう。
lines.english: There had been no eighth year because he had apparently beaten that stubborn old master to a pulp. I never heard the details, but he wasn’t a man who laid hands on anyone without good reason. Call it a youthful indiscretion.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、注文」
lines.english: “Dora. Order.”

lines.japanese: 地鳴りみたいに低い声が放たれた。それを背中で聞いた鳴の肩がびくんと揺れる。
lines.english: His voice rumbled like the earth itself. Behind him, Naru's shoulders jumped.

lines.japanese: 明け方近くになると、この店にも仕事帰りのお水なおねーさんたちが寄ったりするけど、あんまりリピーターにはならない。味はいいのに、カンジ悪げな顔と声と喋り方で損してる。
lines.english: Toward dawn, women coming home from the nightlife trade sometimes stopped here, but few became regulars. The food was excellent; his hostile-looking face, voice, and manner cost him business.

lines.japanese: 「ラーメンふたつ……あ、こいつの油少なめで」
lines.english: “Two bowls... Oh, easy on the oil in hers.”

lines.japanese: おごるつもりはないけど、面倒だから連れの分もまとめて頼んだ。ダイエット仕様で。
lines.english: I had no intention of paying for her, but ordering for both of us was less trouble. I even had hers made diet-friendly.

lines.japanese: 「いいよな」
lines.english: “That okay?”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は小さく頷いて、そのままゆっくり屋台を振りかえった。気付いたメンマが、いかつい顔を不器用にほころばせる。ぺこり、ふたたび鳴の頭が縦に動いた──顔合わせ終了。
lines.english: Naru gave a tiny nod, then slowly turned toward the stall. Menma noticed and awkwardly softened his rugged face. Her head dipped once more. Introductions complete.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、大盛りサービスしてやろうか」
lines.english: “Dora. Want a free upgrade to a large?”

lines.japanese: メンマが屋台の陰から少しだけ体を出した。珍しいことを言う。
lines.english: Menma leaned a little way out from the shadow of the stall. An unusual offer.

lines.japanese: 「なに。なんか、めでたいことでもあったの」
lines.english: “What? Something good happen?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。おまえがここに連れてきたってことは、俺たちに新しい仲間ができたってことだろ」
lines.english: “Yeah. If you brought her here, that means we've got somebody new joining our little circle, right?”

lines.japanese: やつはいかつい表情のまま、かすかに口元を緩めた。俺は背もたれのない椅子の上で片あぐらをかいた。
lines.english: Still wearing his rugged scowl, he let the corners of his mouth relax. I folded one leg beneath me on the backless stool.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、ひとつ大盛り」
lines.english: “Then make one large.”

lines.japanese: 「あいよ」
lines.english: “Coming up.”

lines.japanese: でかい男は承って屋台へ引っこんだ。
lines.english: The big man took the order and ducked back into the stall.

lines.japanese: 向かいの席では、ちんまい女がひとり首を傾げていた。
lines.english: Across the table, the tiny woman tilted her head.

lines.japanese: 「えー、ドラさん大盛りにしなくていいんですか？」
lines.english: “Aren't you getting the large one, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。俺は大盛りだよ。並はおまえのに決まってんだろ、ダイエッター」
lines.english: “Why wouldn’t I? Mine’s the large. Obviously the regular is yours, Miss Diet.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、すみませーん、両方大盛りでお願いしますー」
lines.english: “Excuse me! Could you make them both large, please?”

lines.japanese: 「あいよー」
lines.english: “Coming up.”

lines.japanese: 店主は苦笑した。新しい客も花より団子のいい笑顔。理想的な食卓だ。
lines.english: The owner gave a wry smile. The new customer beamed with the pure joy of someone who chose food over flowers. An ideal table.

lines.japanese: 「やー、ほんと美味しそうな匂いですよねー。ここはもう鳳だけに大盛りですよねー」
lines.english: “It really does smell delicious. And Otori means ‘big bird,’ so naturally I need the big bowl.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いーけどさ、おまえマジに減量する気あんの」
lines.english: “Fine, but are you actually trying to lose weight?”

lines.japanese: 「♪す～すすす～す～」
lines.english: “♪ Soo-so-soo-soo-soo.”

lines.japanese: 俺の呆れた視線を、鳴は気付かないふり＆吹けもしない口笛で受けながした。
lines.english: Naru brushed aside my exasperated stare by pretending not to notice it and faking a whistle she couldn't produce.

lines.japanese: 「太るぞ」
lines.english: “You’ll get fat.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。耳塞いだって意味ねーから」
lines.english: “I told you. Covering your ears changes nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ドラさん丸っこい女性は嫌いですかー」
lines.english: “Do you dislike rounder women, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな話はしてねえよ」
lines.english: “That’s not what we were talking about.”

lines.japanese: でもまあ、食いしんぼうな子供は嫌いじゃない。
lines.english: Still, I didn't dislike a gluttonous kid.

lines.japanese: 「んー！」
lines.english: “Mmm!”

lines.japanese: 鳴は湯気の立つ丼が届けられるや、綺麗に割りバシを割って（たしかに上手かった）俺より先にかぶりついていた。
lines.english: The moment the steaming bowls arrived, Naru split her chopsticks cleanly—she really was good at it—and dug in before I did.

lines.japanese: 「んんー、んんんーっ！」
lines.english: “Mmm! Mmmmm!”

lines.japanese: 「だろ」
lines.english: “Told you.”

lines.japanese: 髪が顔に垂れかかるのなんか気にも留めないで、それでも麺をすする音にはちょっとだけ気を使いながら、鳴は速いテンポで箸を上下させる。
lines.english: She paid no attention to the hair falling across her face, though she was self-conscious enough to keep her slurping quiet. Her chopsticks rose and fell at a brisk tempo.

lines.japanese: 女だてらに気持ちのいい食べっぷりだ。負けてられない。俺はやつが音なんか気にならなくなるぐらいの、さらに大袈裟な音を立ててずるずる吸いこんだ。
lines.english: For a girl, she ate with refreshing gusto. I couldn't let her beat me. I sucked up my noodles with an even more extravagant slurp, loud enough to make her stop worrying about the noise.

lines.japanese: 「やー、やっぱり大盛りにしてもらって良かったですねー」
lines.english: “I'm so glad we had him make them large.”

lines.japanese: 「カロリーも大盛りだけどな」
lines.english: “That goes for the calories too.”

lines.japanese: ずるっ！　ずるっ！　ずるっ！
lines.english: Slurp! Slurp! Slurp!

lines.japanese: 女は現実から逃避して食事に打ちこんだ。
lines.english: The woman fled reality and devoted herself to her meal.

lines.japanese: 「これも」
lines.english: “This too.”

lines.japanese: 大男が鈍牛のようにのしのしやってきて、テーブルの中央に陶器の皿を置いていった。ザーサイとチャーシューと輪切りの煮玉子が盛りつけられていた。
lines.english: The huge man lumbered over like an ox and set a ceramic plate in the middle of the table. It held pickled mustard greens, roast pork, and slices of seasoned egg.

lines.japanese: 「なにこれ。頼んでねえよ」
lines.english: “What's this? We didn't order it.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。パルからだ」
lines.english: “No. It's from Paru.”

lines.japanese: 「パルさん？　あァ？　ちょっと待てコラてめ、なに報告してんだよ」
lines.english: “Paru? Hey, wait, asshole. What are you reporting to her for?”

lines.japanese: 「たまたま用があって電話しただけだ。まあ、ご馳走ンなっとけよ」
lines.english: “I happened to have business with her and called. Just enjoy the treat.”

lines.japanese: メンマは俺を無視して、鳴に優しく（たぶん）微笑みかけた。鳴は慌てて箸を置いて、かしこまったお辞儀をした。借りてきた猫みたいだった。
lines.english: Ignoring me, Menma smiled gently—or probably gently—at Naru. She hurriedly put down her chopsticks and bowed with perfect formality, suddenly as meek as a kitten.

lines.japanese: 俺は鈍牛が牛舎に戻るのを待ってから言った。
lines.english: I waited until the ox had lumbered back to his stall before I spoke.

lines.japanese: 「だからビビんなって。あいつアレだからアレ、気は優しくて力持ち」
lines.english: “I told you, don't be scared. He's just a gentle giant.”

lines.japanese: 「あーはい、そういうわけではないんですけどー。ほら私、基本的には引っ込み思案な女の子じゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Oh, no, it’s not that. You know how I’m basically a shy girl who keeps to herself?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、引っ込み思案な女の子は、自分のこと引っ込み思案な女の子とかアピんねーだろ」
lines.english: “A shy and retiring girl doesn't advertise herself as a shy and retiring girl.”

lines.japanese: 「でもー、なんか最近ー、初対面のひとと会うときすっごく緊張しちゃうんですよー」
lines.english: “But, like, lately I get really nervous whenever I meet someone for the first time.”

lines.japanese: ああ、そういや言われてみれば……たしかにクレープ屋で初めて俺と目が合ったときも、鳴はそんな感じだったような記憶が。まあ、気持ちは分かるかもしれない。
lines.english: Come to think of it... I vaguely remembered Naru acting that way when our eyes first met at the crêpe stand. I could understand the feeling, perhaps.

lines.japanese: 「繊細な心を持ったガラスの少女なんですー」
lines.english: “I'm a fragile girl of glass.”

lines.japanese: まあ、気持ちは分かるかもしれない。
lines.english: I could understand the feeling, perhaps.

lines.japanese: 「あたかもボヘミアの伝統工芸のようですよー」
lines.english: “Rather like a work of traditional Bohemian glass.”

lines.japanese: いや、それは分からない。
lines.english: No. I couldn't understand that.

lines.japanese: 「でも、ほんとにドラさんってお友達多いんですねー」
lines.english: “But you really do have a lot of friends, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだそれ。ラーメン屋クレープ屋の一人や二人で」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that supposed to mean? One ramen guy and one crêpe lady?”

lines.japanese: 「だってほらー、他にもうちの兄ですとか、兄の友人ですとかー」
lines.english: “There's also my brother, and his friends...”

lines.japanese: ありゃ友達じゃねえ。
lines.english: Those weren't friends.

lines.japanese: 俺は遅れて届けられたパルさんからのプレゼントを、いくつか丼の中に放りこんだ。
lines.english: I dropped several pieces of Paru's belated gift into my bowl.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん言ってましたよー」
lines.english: “Paru told me something.”

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんは自分から壁を作って、勝手に一匹狼気取ってるだけだって。ドラさんを友達だと思ってるひとはたくさんいるのにって」
lines.english: “She said you build the walls yourself and then play lone wolf. That lots of people think of you as a friend.”

lines.japanese: 「安っぽい分析」
lines.english: “Bargain-bin pop psychology.”

lines.japanese: でも、ゲーセンの心理解析マシーンなんかよりはマシかもしれない。
lines.english: Though it might be better than one of those personality-analysis machines at the arcade.

lines.japanese: ずる、ずる、ずるっ……俺たちはほとんど相手の目も見ず、ちょっと熱いぐらいの麺をすすりながら話を続ける。
lines.english: Slurp, slurp, slurp... We continued talking over noodles still a little too hot to eat, scarcely looking each other in the eye.

lines.japanese: 「でもそれな、トモダチっつーか、トモダチいない変なやつらが消去法的に寄りあつまってるだけだから」
lines.english: “But see, it isn't exactly friendship. It's just a bunch of friendless weirdos getting shoved together by process of elimination.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、遠足の班決め……でしたっけー」
lines.english: “Oh. Like choosing groups for a field trip... Was that it?”

lines.japanese: 前に俺が使ったたとえ話を、やつはまだ覚えていたみたいだ。社会の班決めから取りこぼされたぼくたち、っていうそんな話。
lines.english: She apparently still remembered the analogy I had used before: all of us left over when society chose its groups.

lines.japanese: 「あれってけっこう残酷なシステムですよねー」
lines.english: “That's quite a cruel system, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「経験者は語るか」
lines.english: “Speaking from experience?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、まー」
lines.english: “Well... yes.”

lines.japanese: 否定のツッコミが返ってこなかった。くだらないことを言ってしまった。やっぱり俺には冗談の才能がないみたいだ（小娘の一面が垣間見えて、多少の親近感が湧いたりはしたけれど）。
lines.english: She didn’t come back with a denial. Stupid thing to say. Apparently I really had no gift for jokes. (Though seeing this vulnerable side of the kid did make me feel a shade closer to her.)

lines.japanese: 会話が止まって、俺たちはしばらくずるずる音を立てていた。
lines.english: Our conversation stopped, and for a while we did nothing but slurp.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、ドラさんの周りの『変なひと』って、たとえばどんなひとなんですか」
lines.english: “Um, Dora, what sort of ‘strange people’ do you have around you?”

lines.japanese: 鳴が聞いてきた。
lines.english: Naru asked.

lines.japanese: 「変なひと」
lines.english: “A strange person.”

lines.japanese: 俺は丼から目を上げないまま、箸の先で正面の女を指した。
lines.english: Without lifting my eyes from the bowl, I pointed the tips of my chopsticks at the woman across from me.

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「納得してるし」
lines.english: “And she agrees.”

lines.japanese: 俺は犬みたいに丼へ口をつけ、脂の浮いた濃い汁をずずずと啜った。
lines.english: I put my mouth to the bowl like a dog and noisily drank the rich broth, grease shimmering on its surface.

lines.japanese: 器のふちに箸を置く音が聞こえた。鳴は両手をテーブルの下に垂らして、柳木原の夜空を仰いでいた。
lines.english: I heard her chopsticks come to rest against the rim. Naru let both hands hang beneath the table and gazed up at the night sky over Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、なんとなくー……分かってきました」
lines.english: “Ah. Yes. I think I'm beginning to get it... a little.”

lines.japanese: 「なにが」
lines.english: “Understand what?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、いろいろ……いま私が緊張しないで普通に話してることとか」
lines.english: “Well, various things... Like why I can talk normally now without feeling nervous.”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 普通ってなんだ。と思ったけど茶々は入れなかった。代わりにテーブルの上にあった小瓶を掴んで、白コショウをたっぷり入れた。
lines.english: What was *normally* supposed to mean? I wondered, but didn't interrupt. Instead, I picked up the small bottle on the table and added a generous dose of white pepper.

lines.japanese: 自分の方が済むと、俺はその小瓶を鳴に差しむけて目で訊いた。やつは遠慮がちに微笑んでこくんと頷いた。俺は軽く二振りしてやった。
lines.english: When I was done with mine, I held the bottle toward Naru and asked with my eyes. She smiled timidly and gave a tiny nod. I shook it lightly twice over her bowl.

lines.japanese: 「私、兄と離れて暮らしてたって言ったじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “I told you I used to live apart from my brother, didn't I?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あー、そういや言ってたな」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, right. You did.”

lines.japanese: 俺はコショウの瓶を元の位置に戻して夜食を再開した。鳴はまだ箸を取らなかった。
lines.english: I returned the pepper to its place and resumed my late-night meal. Naru still hadn't picked up her chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 「父の仕事の都合で去年まで……えーと、六年間ほどですか、私ネーデルランドにいたんですよー」
lines.english: “Because of my father's work, until last year I spent... let me see, about six years in Nederland.”

lines.japanese: 「何それ。何県にあんの、その遊園地」
lines.english: “What's that? Which prefecture is that amusement park in?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、えーとオランダです」
lines.english: “Oh. Um, the Netherlands.”

lines.japanese: 「オランダって、え、外国のオランダ？」
lines.english: “The Netherlands? You mean the foreign country?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですねー」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、赤線とか大麻が合法の、あのオランダ？」
lines.english: “The Netherlands where pot and the red-light district are legal?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、珍しいですねドラさん。大抵のひと、まずチューリップか風車って言いますよ」
lines.english: “How unusual, Dora. Most people mention tulips or windmills first.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。なに、じゃあおまえオランダ語とか喋れんの」
lines.english: “Seriously? So you can speak Dutch and everything?”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえ、日本語で生活できる環境でしたから、それは日本人学校の授業で習った程度です。ただ、父が昔から英語の家庭教師を付けてくれてましてー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. Japanese was enough for daily life, so I only learned as much Dutch as they taught at Japanese school. But my father had arranged a private English tutor for me from an early age.”

lines.japanese: 「英語ってイギリス語？　え、じゃあおまえイギリス語できんの」
lines.english: “English, as in England-language? So you can speak England-language?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、えーと、先生はアメリカのひとだったので本場のクイーンズイングリッシュではないんですけれどもー」
lines.english: “Well, the tutor was American, so it wasn't exactly authentic Queen's English.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……なんかよく分かんねーけど、要するになに、オランダの遊園地でアメリカ人からイギリス語を習ってたってことか」
lines.english: “Uh... I don't really get it. Basically, you learned England-language from an American at this Dutch amusement park.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、微妙に違いますけどそれでいいです」
lines.english: “Yes. That's subtly wrong, but close enough.”

lines.japanese: 「それで今年の春、進学を機に日本へ戻ってきたんですけど……やー、新しい学校で、始まって早々ちょっとやっちゃいましてー」
lines.english: “Then I returned to Japan this spring to continue my education... and, well, I messed up a little almost as soon as I started at my new school.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は口を横に引っぱって笑った。なんだか、酔ったプラチナが映画スターを目指して田舎を飛びだしたいきさつをネタにするときのような顔だった。
lines.english: Naru stretched her mouth sideways in a smile. It was the sort of face Platinum made when he got drunk and turned his flight from the sticks to become a movie star into a comedy routine.

lines.japanese: 「４月のいちばん最初の英語の授業のときだったんですけどー。隣りの席の子が、えーと、なにかの単語を間違った意味で覚えてたんで、こう、横からひょろっと教えてあげたんですねー」
lines.english: “It was during our very first English lesson in April. The girl beside me had learned the wrong meaning for some word, so I casually leaned over and corrected her.”

lines.japanese: 「や、ほんと、純粋に親切心からですよ？」
lines.english: “Honestly, it was pure kindness. You understand?”

lines.japanese: やつは丼の両脇にふたつのこぶしを置いて身を乗りだした。俺はラーメンを食いながら頷いた。
lines.english: She planted both fists beside her bowl and leaned toward me. I nodded as I ate.

lines.japanese: ずる、ずる、ずるるっ……。
lines.english: Slurp, slurp, sluuurp...

lines.japanese: 「でもその瞬間……まー、なんと言いますか、教室の空気が変わったというやつですか……やー、むしろ空気を読めなかったのは私なんですけどー」
lines.english: “But at that instant... Well, how should I put it? The air in the classroom changed. Though I suppose I was the one who failed to read it.”

lines.japanese: 金持ちの嬢で帰国子女。頭いい。運動できる。見てくれ悪くない。キャラちょっとフシギ系──なるほど、麻雀だったら合わせて６翻、バンバン付けて倍満だ。ちょっと条件が揃いすぎてる。
lines.english: A rich girl raised overseas. Smart. Athletic. Not bad-looking. A little eccentric—in mahjong terms, that made six scoring doubles; add the automatic two and she was a double-limit hand. Far too many winning conditions lined up at once.

lines.japanese: 陳腐な想像力しか持たない俺でも、そのときの「教室の空気」ってやつは肌に痛いほど感じることができた。去年まで鳴のいたところがどうだったかは知らないが、ここはそういう風土の国だ。経験者は語る。
lines.english: Even with an imagination as limited as mine, I could feel that “classroom atmosphere” sting my skin. I didn’t know what the place Naru had lived until last year was like, but this was the kind of country Japan was. Spoken from experience.

lines.japanese: 「んー、いま思いかえすに……どーもあの辺りからこう、なにかが少しずつずれ始めたんですよねー。そしたら一学期が終わって二学期も終わって、なんかふと気付いたら私、いまひとりも友達いないんですよー」
lines.english: “Looking back... I think that was where things began slipping slightly out of alignment. Then the first term ended, and the second ended, and one day I happened to notice that I didn't have a single friend.”

lines.japanese: 「クラスの子はみんな、付属からのエスカレーター組とか地元のグループとかで、なんとなーく最初から輪が出来てるわけじゃないですかー。でも私ほら余所者なんでー、元々の友達もいないですしー」
lines.english: “Everyone in my class already had their circles from the affiliated school or their local groups. They were more or less formed from the beginning. But I was an outsider, you see, so I didn't have any old friends there.”

lines.japanese: 俺は黙々とラーメンを食いながら、だけどたまに目を合わせて、話を聞いてることだけは知らしめた。麺ひとすすりごとに見たやつの表情は、頬の筋肉を強張らせて形成された息詰まるような笑顔だった。
lines.english: I ate my ramen in silence, meeting her eyes now and then to show I was listening. Each time I looked up between mouthfuls, her cheek muscles were still locked into the same suffocating smile.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。じゃあガッコつまんねーな」
lines.english: “Huh. Then school must suck.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、そーですねー。軌道修正に必死な時期もありましたけど、それも裏目裏目でしたしー」
lines.english: “Yes, I suppose it does. There was a time when I desperately tried to correct my course, but every effort backfired.”

lines.japanese: 温かくない視線の中でも、上手く立ちまわれさえすれば徐々にでもその温度を変えることは出来たかもしれない。しかし──何でもソツなくこなせそうな鳴も、その辺だけは不得手だったみたいだ。
lines.english: Even beneath those cold looks, she might gradually have warmed them if she had known how to handle herself. But that one thing, apparently, was beyond even Naru, who seemed capable of doing everything else without a stumble.

lines.japanese: 「なんだかもう疲れはててしまったので、残りの学園生活はひっそりと呼吸だけしながら生きながらえるとします。ええ、もう、あたかも耳を塞いでラーメンを食すように」
lines.english: “I'm thoroughly exhausted now, so I intend to survive the rest of my school life quietly, doing nothing but breathing. Yes. Rather like eating ramen with one's ears covered.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はいったん言葉を切って、ラーメンをひと口、ふた口すすった。
lines.english: Naru broke off and slurped one mouthful, then another.

lines.japanese: しかしまたすぐに箸を置いた。
lines.english: But almost immediately, she set down her chopsticks again.

lines.japanese: 「──なんですけどー、でもー」
lines.english: “—That's what I intend, but still...”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: やつがまだ自虐的な言葉を続けそうだったので、俺は強引に割りこんだ。
lines.english: She seemed ready to continue the self-mockery, so I cut her off.

lines.japanese: 「そーゆーのもアリなんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Nothing wrong with living that way.”

lines.japanese: 「はー？　えー、そーですかー？」
lines.english: “Huh? You really think so?”

lines.japanese: 「たぶんな」
lines.english: “Probably.”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつの保護者でも教員でもないから、無責任なことを言った。無責任だけど、でも適当にあしらったつもりはなかった。鳴の選んだ道はちょっと俺のにカブッてるかもしれない。
lines.english: I wasn’t her guardian or her teacher, so it was irresponsible of me to say it. Irresponsible, yes, but I hadn’t meant to brush her off. The path Naru had chosen might overlap slightly with mine.

lines.japanese: ──ところで話は変わるけど、おまえは飛べない鳥にどんな選択肢があるか考えたことがあるだろうか。
lines.english: —Changing the subject: have you ever considered what choices remain to a bird that cannot fly?

lines.japanese: たとえばタカシは、見上げることをやめて空の高さを忘れた。
lines.english: Takashi, for example, stopped looking upward and forgot the height of the sky.

lines.japanese: たとえば鷲介は、必死で飛べるふりをして鳥の群れに潜りこんだ。
lines.english: Shusuke, for example, desperately pretended he could fly and slipped into the flock.

lines.japanese: たとえば俺は、世界の底を駆けぬけるための強靭な脚を身につけた。乾いたサバンナを疾走する鳥がいたっていいじゃないか。
lines.english: I, for example, built powerful legs with which to race across the bottom of the world. Why shouldn't there be a bird that sprinted over the dry savanna?

lines.japanese: でも以前には、まるで誰かの兄貴みたいに、爪を研いで空を睨んでいたやんちゃな時期もあったんだ。ダセぇだろ、まったく、てんで笑えない昔話──
lines.english: But once, like somebody's big brother, I too had a reckless season when I sharpened my claws and glared at the sky. Pathetic, isn't it? An old story without a single laugh in it—

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、君はどうしてそんなに強くなりたいんだね」
lines.english: “Hayato, why do you want so badly to become strong?”

lines.japanese: 「ひみつ」
lines.english: “Secret.”

lines.japanese: 「話したくないことなのかな」
lines.english: “Is it something you don't want to discuss?”

lines.japanese: 「話さなきゃいけねーことなのかな」
lines.english: “Is it something I have to discuss?”

lines.japanese: ふてくされてるガキに、じいさんは辛抱づよく微笑んだ。
lines.english: The old man smiled patiently at the sulking child.

lines.japanese: 「本当のことを話したくないなら、君は私に嘘をついてあしらうことができる。だから無理に話せと言っても意味はないだろうね」
lines.english: “If you don't want to tell me the truth, you can always lie and brush me aside. So there would be little point in forcing you to speak.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 余裕ぶって見せてはいたけど、あのときの俺は、焦りにも似た高揚感にひどく疼いていた。
lines.english: I had put on an air of indifference, but at the time a feverish exhilaration almost like panic throbbed beneath my skin.

lines.japanese: 王者不在だった日本ボクシング界に一年振りの世界チャンプが誕生して、翌日のアルバトロスビジョンにもその試合のハイライトは繰りかえし映しだされた。
lines.english: After a year without a champion, Japanese boxing had produced a new world titleholder. The next day, Albatross Vision played the highlights of the bout again and again.

lines.japanese: メキシコ生まれのハードパンチャーをリングに沈め、絶望的とまで囁かれた下馬評を覆したのは技巧派の日本人。その洗練されたしなやかな動きは、習わぬ経を読みはじめた門前の小僧に強い衝撃を刻みつけた。
lines.english: A Japanese technician had floored a Mexican-born power puncher and overturned odds said to be hopeless. Like the temple boy who learns his sutras without a lesson, I had absorbed enough to be stunned by the champion’s polished, supple movement.

lines.japanese: 一夜にして世の嘲笑を歓声に変えてしまった男は、無数のマイクロフォンに向かって、逆境こそが自分をここまで導いたと男泣きに泣いた。
lines.english: Overnight, the man had transformed public scorn into cheers. Facing a thicket of microphones, he wept unashamedly and said adversity had carried him this far.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれを格好いいとは思わなかった。ただ、ひどく焦れた。俺だってきっとそうなれるはずだと、幼い野心を滾らせていた。
lines.english: I didn’t think he looked cool. I only felt unbearably restless. Surely I could become that too, I thought, childish ambition seething inside me.

lines.japanese: じいさんはなぜ強くなりたいかと問うた。すこし考えてから、俺はその理由を抽象的に告げた。
lines.english: The old man had asked why I wanted to become strong. After thinking briefly, I answered in the abstract.

lines.japanese: 「勝つために」
lines.english: “To win.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは表情を変えず、ただ祭壇の彫像みたいに固まったまま、しばらく俺の目を覗きこんでいた。
lines.english: His expression did not change. He remained motionless as a statue on an altar and gazed into my eyes for some time.

lines.japanese: 「フツーだろ。問題ある？」
lines.english: “That's normal, isn't it? Is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「いいや。障害や困難に立ちむかう勇気は大切だね。私はそういう男の子が大好きだ」
lines.english: “No. Courage in the face of obstacles and hardship is important. I'm very fond of boys like that.”

lines.japanese: その声は険しいのか優しいのかよく分からなかった。
lines.english: I couldn't tell whether his voice was stern or gentle.

lines.japanese: 「でも思い過ごしかな、君の瞳には憎悪と怨嗟……ふむ、つまり、誰かをやっつけてやりたいと思う気持ちが見え隠れしているんだ」
lines.english: “But perhaps it's my imagination. In your eyes, I catch glimpses of hatred and rancor... In plainer words, the desire to beat somebody up.”

lines.japanese: 真に卓抜した洞察力でガキの内面を覗きこんだのか、それともあらかじめ俺について幾ばくかの知識を得ていたのか。それはいまでも分からないけれど、俺は図星を突かれてすこし腹立たしい気分になった。
lines.english: Whether he had peered inside the child with extraordinary insight or learned something about me beforehand, I still don’t know. But he had hit the mark, and it made me angry.

lines.japanese: 「だったらなに。稽古やめんの」
lines.english: “So what? You gonna stop training me?”

lines.japanese: 開きなおった態度を装いながら、長い机の下でちっぽけなこぶしを握りしめた。俺には味方なんていない。そう思うと暗い激情がこみあげてきた。
lines.english: Pretending defiance, I clenched a tiny fist beneath the long table. Nobody was on my side. The thought sent a dark fury surging through me.

lines.japanese: 今にして思えば、それがじいさんの言う憎悪と怨嗟ってやつだったんだろう。誰かをやっつけてやりたいと思う気持ち。俺は倍ちかい体格差のある老人を低い視点から睨んでいた。
lines.english: Looking back, that must have been the hatred and rancor the old man meant. The desire to hurt someone. From my low vantage, I glared at an old man nearly twice my size.

lines.japanese: 「仕方ねぇだろ」
lines.english: “What choice do I have?”

lines.japanese: 「俺が強くならなきゃ、誰が俺たちを守るんだ」
lines.english: “If I don't get strong, who's going to protect us?”

lines.japanese: 脅したつもりはなかった。逆だ。きっと俺は哀れんでほしかったんだろう。
lines.english: I hadn't meant it as a threat. The opposite. I probably wanted his pity.

lines.japanese: じいさんは言葉もなく、俺に墨色の背中を向けた。
lines.english: Without a word, the old man turned his ink-dark back to me.

lines.japanese: 「覚えておきなさい。剣を取るものは皆、剣で滅びる」
lines.english: “Remember this. All they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.”

lines.japanese: しかし、その大きな体が告げたのは、痛烈な拒絶の言葉ではなかった。
lines.english: But the words from that broad back were no brutal rejection.

lines.japanese: 「私は君の剣を鍛えているつもりはない。心を守る盾を研いているんだ」
lines.english: “I am not trying to forge your sword. I am polishing a shield to protect your heart.”

lines.japanese: そして、厳然たる師の声で告げた。
lines.english: Then he spoke in the austere voice of a master.

lines.japanese: 「始めよう。準備運動をして待っていなさい」
lines.english: “Let's begin. Warm up and wait for me.”

lines.japanese: 俺は両手で器を捧げもち、店主自慢の特製スープを喉に流しこんだ。鼻にスパイスが利きすぎてくしゃみが出そうだった。
lines.english: I raised the bowl in both hands and poured the proprietor’s special broth down my throat. The spices hit my nose so hard I nearly sneezed.

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」
鳴は思いだしたように箸を手に取ったが、麺をいったんスープの中から揚げただけで、なかなかそれを口の中へは運ばなかった。
lines.english: Naru seemed to remember her chopsticks at last. She picked them up and lifted a tangle of noodles from the broth, but couldn’t bring it to her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「もしあのとき、あの一言を口にしてなかったら、私いまごろみんなとクレープでも食べてるんですかねー」
lines.english: “If I hadn't said that one thing back then, do you think I'd be eating crêpes with everyone now?”

lines.japanese: そうかもしれないし、そうじゃないかもしれない。意味のない仮定だ。たられば話じゃ百点棒一本返ってこないって、むかし立ち読みした麻雀指南書にも書いてあった。
lines.english: Perhaps she would. Perhaps she wouldn’t. It was a meaningless hypothetical. A mahjong guide I once browsed without buying had said that no *if only* could win back even one lousy hundred-point stick.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあその場合、俺とラーメンは食ってねえわけだな」
lines.english: “In that case, you wouldn't be eating ramen with me now.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そかー、そうですよねー」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. That’s true.”

lines.japanese: 「なら、これで良かったじゃん」
lines.english: “Then this worked out fine.”

lines.japanese: 俺は顔を上げずに、具ごとずるずる麺をかっこみながら言った。
lines.english: Without raising my face, I said it while shoveling noodles and toppings into my mouth.

lines.japanese: 「はい、良かったです」
lines.english: “Yes. It worked out fine.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は語尾を伸ばさないではっきり答えた。
lines.english: Naru answered clearly, without drawing out the final syllable.

lines.japanese: 「めでたしめでたし」
lines.english: “And they lived happily ever after.”

lines.japanese: 「たはは」
lines.english: “Ah-ha-ha.”

lines.japanese: 目が合うと、やつは照れくさそうに笑った。だから俺は茶化してやった。
lines.english: When our eyes met, she smiled with shy embarrassment. So I made a joke of it for her.

lines.japanese: 「例えるならアレだな。切る牌を間違って困ってたら、次のツモでドラ引いて結果オーライって話。ドラだけにな」
lines.english: “It's like discarding the wrong tile, thinking you've screwed up, then drawing the bonus tile next turn and coming out ahead. My name's Dora; of course I'm the bonus.”

lines.japanese: 俺は上手いことを言った。
lines.english: I had said something clever.

lines.japanese: 「あー、すみません私、麻雀はちょっと分からないんでー」
lines.english: “Oh, I'm sorry. I don't really understand mahjong.”

lines.japanese: 「フザケンナ」
lines.english: “You've gotta be kidding me.”

lines.japanese: こぶしの底で軽くテーブルを叩く。俺たちは慣れた空気を取りもどして、食べやすくなったラーメンみたいな温度の視線をぶつけ合った。
lines.english: I tapped the table lightly with the heel of my fist. We slipped back into our old rhythm and met each other's eyes with the easy warmth of ramen cooled just enough to eat.

lines.japanese: 「あー、やー、すみません。なんか麺がのびちゃうような話になってましたねー」
lines.english: “Sorry. Somehow we got onto the kind of subject that leaves your noodles going soft.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はようやく食事を再開した。俺は箸の先でゆで卵の黄身をぐちゃぐちゃに掻きまぜながら言った。
lines.english: At last, Naru resumed eating. I mashed the boiled egg yolk into the broth with the tips of my chopsticks and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「いや、でも、俺もなんとなく分かったかも」
lines.english: “Still, I think I understand something too.”

lines.japanese: 「はー。何がですか」
lines.english: “Oh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「なんつーかアレ……俺さ、あんま、おまえウザくねーみたい」
lines.english: “It's like... I don't find you all that annoying.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、『あまりうざくない』ですか」
lines.english: “Oh. ‘Not all that annoying.’”

lines.japanese: 鳴は誉められたんだか貶されたんだかよく分からない顔をした。俺は自分の箸でやつの丼を鳴らした。
lines.english: Naru looked unsure whether she had been praised or insulted. I tapped her bowl with my chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 「おー、こら、いちいち止まんねーでいいから。まずくなんねーうちに食ってやれよ」
lines.english: “Hey. Come on, you don’t have to stop every time. Eat it before it stops tasting good.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、すみません」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: やつは思いだしたように箸を入れ、つるりつるりと静かに食事を再開した。
lines.english: Apparently remembering she had food in front of her, she dipped her chopsticks back into the bowl and quietly resumed eating, noodles slipping smoothly between her lips.

lines.japanese: 「まぁ、アレかな。『あんまり』っつーか？」
lines.english: “Well, maybe ‘not all that’ isn't right.”

lines.japanese: 俺はスープから揚げた麺を、空中で何度か上下させて息をひとつふたつ吹きかけた。
lines.english: I lifted some noodles from the broth, bobbed them several times in the air, and blew on them once, twice.

lines.japanese: 「ぶっちゃけ、ぜんぜんウザくねーんだけどさ」
lines.english: “Honestly, I don't find you annoying at all.”

lines.japanese: 言うと同時に頭を落としてかぶりついた。ずるずるだ。
lines.english: The moment I said it, I dropped my head, bit into the noodles, and slurped.

lines.japanese: しかしラーメン音が自分のものしか聞こえてこない。俺は顔を上げた。
lines.english: But the only ramen noises I heard were my own. I looked up.

lines.japanese: 鳴は行儀の悪い子供みたく、口から麺の束を垂らしたまま固まっていた。
lines.english: Naru had frozen like an ill-mannered child, a bundle of noodles dangling from her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「うわ、なんだおまえ、きったねぇな。なに止まってんだよ」
lines.english: “Ugh, look at you. That's disgusting. Why'd you stop?”

lines.japanese: やつは目を見張ったまま麺を噛みちぎり、箸に挟まれていた残りをスープの中に落とした。
lines.english: Eyes wide, she bit through the noodles and let the rest fall from her chopsticks into the broth.

lines.japanese: 「……あの、それは告白ですか」
lines.english: “...Was that a love confession?”

lines.japanese: 俺は小娘の脳天に垂直チョップを一発埋めこんだ。
lines.english: I buried a vertical chop in the top of the little girl's head.

lines.japanese: 「耳鼻科行け。もしくは心療内科行け」
lines.english: “See an ear, nose, and throat doctor. Or a shrink.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ？」
lines.english: “Heh-heh?”

lines.japanese: やつは唇に指を添えて流し目をよこす。なんだこりゃ。も、ずるずるだ。
lines.english: She touched a finger to her lips and cast me a sidelong glance. What was this supposed to be? I went back to slurping.

lines.japanese: 「……ふ～う。ごっそさん」
lines.english: “...Phew. That hit the spot.”

lines.japanese: 俺は空っぽになった器を置いてテーブルの端へ滑らせた。
lines.english: I set down the empty bowl and slid it to the edge of the table.

lines.japanese: 麺は最後の一本まで綺麗にたいらげた。イイカンジに体が温まってる。
lines.english: I had polished off every last noodle. My body was pleasantly warm.

lines.japanese: 冬は寒いけど、寒いからこそ温かいラーメンの美味さが際立つんだよな。捨てたもんじゃないだろ、冬。そこまで来てるんだぜ、冬。
lines.english: Winter was cold, but the cold was what made hot ramen taste so good. Winter wasn’t entirely worthless. And it was right around the corner.

lines.japanese: 「わ、早っ！」
lines.english: “Whoa, that was fast!”

lines.japanese: 鳴は首を伸ばして俺のドンブリを覗きこみ、それが空っぽだと分かるとあわてて食のスピードを上げた。
lines.english: Naru craned her neck to peer into my bowl. Once she saw it was empty, she hurriedly picked up the pace.

lines.japanese: ずるっ、ずるっ、ずるるるっ……。
lines.english: Slurp, slurp, sluuurp...

lines.japanese: 「ああ、おまえさ」
lines.english: “Hey, listen.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁ、ふぁいっ！」
lines.english: “Y-yef!”

lines.japanese: 「……いや、べつに、ゆっくり食ってていいけど」
lines.english: “...Never mind. You can eat slowly.”

lines.japanese: 俺は椅子の縁に手を引っかけ、背もたれのない中空にぐっと背中を反らせた。
lines.english: I gripped the edge of the stool and leaned back against the nonexistent backrest.

lines.japanese: 「おまえさ、またなんか、つまんねードジかましてネタでも出来たらここ来いよ」
lines.english: “If you screw up in some stupid way again and come away with another story to tell, come here.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶぁ？」
lines.english: “Bwuh?”

lines.japanese: 「俺いなくても、パルさんの言う変なやつらってのが誰かしかいるかもしんねーし。おまえ面白れーから、すぐ連中に気に入られんだろうな」
lines.english: “Even if I'm not around, one of those weird people Paru mentioned probably will be. You're funny. They'll take to you right away.”

lines.japanese: この薄汚いテーブルは、寂しがり屋のダチョウやペンギンが身を寄せあってキィキィ騒ぐにはうってつけの聖域なんだ。
lines.english: This grimy table was the perfect sanctuary for lonely ostriches and penguins to huddle together and squawk.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、たぶんエージかプラチナあたりに、しょーもない仇名付けられるとは思うけど」
lines.english: “Though Eiji or Platinum will probably stick you with some stupid nickname.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶぁ……ぶぁい。ばびがどうごばいばず！」
lines.english: “Yef... Yef. Thag you very much!”

lines.japanese: 鳴はだらしなく口から麺の束を垂らしたまま返事をした。ひでえツラ。こいつはどんなに辛くても笑っていられる強いやつなんだろうなと思った。
lines.english: Naru answered with a sloppy bundle of noodles hanging from her mouth. What a terrible face. I thought she must be strong—the kind of person who could keep smiling no matter how much it hurt.

lines.japanese: そしたら、もうひとつ俺に気まぐれが起こった。
lines.english: Then another whim took me.

lines.japanese: 「おまえさ、あさって……日曜ってなんか用事ある？」
lines.english: “You doing anything the day after tomorrow? Sunday?”
“Bweh?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ヒマだったらちょっと犬の散歩付きあってもらおーと思ったんだけど」
lines.english: “If you're free, I thought you could come walk a dog with me.”

lines.japanese: 「日曜夜７時、パルクレープ集合。まー、べつに、来ても来なくてもどっちでも」
lines.english: “Seven Sunday night. Meet at Paru Crêpes. Doesn't matter whether you come or not.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は口の中のものがなくなるまで、じっと俺の目を凝視しながら顎を動かしていた。
lines.english: Naru worked her jaw while staring steadily into my eyes, waiting until her mouth was empty.

lines.japanese: もごもご、もごもご……（咀嚼）
lines.english: Munch, munch... (Chewing.)

lines.japanese: も、ご……（咀嚼中断）
lines.english: Mun... (Chewing suspended.)

lines.japanese: ……ごくん（嚥下）
lines.english: ...Gulp. (Swallowed.)

lines.japanese: 「つまりそれはデートですね」
lines.english: “In other words, it's a date.”

lines.japanese: 「仕事です」
lines.english: “It's a job.”

lines.japanese: 「照れてる照れてる」
lines.english: “You're blushing, you're blushing.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「告白、そしてデートのお誘い。次はいよいよ何をしでかすんでしょう」
lines.english: “A confession, followed by an invitation to a date. What will you do next, I wonder?”

lines.japanese: 「いい。もうおまえ来んな。ぜってー来んな」
lines.english: “Forget it. Don't come. Do not come.”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえ！　はい、了解です！　日曜７時パルクレープ了解です！」
lines.english: “Oh, no! Yes, understood! Seven o'clock Sunday at Paru Crêpes. Understood!”

lines.japanese: 「いいっつの。来なくていいっつの」
lines.english: “Forget it. I told you not to come.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、素直じゃないわねボウヤ」
lines.english: “Heh-heh. Why can't you be honest with yourself, little boy?”

lines.japanese: 「うー、るー、せー！」
lines.english: “Shut! Up!”

lines.japanese: びしびしびしびし……びしびしびしびし……。
lines.english: Chop-chop-chop-chop... chop-chop-chop-chop...

lines.japanese: 俺は両手を使って垂直チョップの雨を降らせた。
lines.english: I used both hands to rain vertical chops upon her.

lines.japanese: びしびしびしびし……びしびしびしびし……。
lines.english: Chop-chop-chop-chop... chop-chop-chop-chop...

lines.japanese: 「あー、あれですかねー、やっぱり秋の終わりに吹く夜風は何故だか誰しもをひと恋しくさせてしまうんですかねー」
lines.english: “Ah, maybe the night wind at the end of autumn just makes everyone long for company for some reason.”

lines.japanese: 「うぉ、すげえ。こいつ、こんなチョップぶちこまれてんのにフツーに喋ってる。超すげえ」
lines.english: “Whoa, amazing. I'm chopping the hell out of her, and she's talking like nothing's happening. Incredible.”

lines.japanese: 「恋は盲目ですよー」
lines.english: “Love is blind.”

lines.japanese: それから俺は、鳴を相手にしばらく時間を潰して……最後に駅まで見送ったあと、いつもの現場へ入った。
lines.english: After that, I killed some time with Naru... and once I had seen her to the station, I reported to my usual job site.

lines.japanese: プリン頭たちがラーメン屋に消えた休憩時間、俺はひとり高速道路の冷たい橋脚に寄りかかって、鳴と食ったあのあったかい味を思いだした。
lines.english: During break, when the crew with the grown-out dye jobs disappeared into a ramen shop, I leaned alone against a cold concrete pier beneath the expressway and remembered the warmth of that ramen with Naru.

lines.japanese: 麺は自家製、スープは無化調。ぜったいメンマのラーメンの方が美味いと思うんだ。
lines.english: Homemade noodles. MSG-free broth. Menma's ramen was definitely better.

lines.japanese: ざまあみやがれ。
lines.english: So there.
